candidates.rule: Behaviour changes to public provider hook methods (e.g. return-value shape, filtering of entries) must be documented in the provider's `docs/changelog.rst` under the next release version.
candidates.trigger: diff alters the return value or filtering logic of an existing public provider hook method without adding an entry to `docs/changelog.rst`

candidates.rule: Do not silently change the API contract of an existing async hook method; if new behaviour (e.g. recursive walk, full-path return) is desired, add an explicit flag parameter or a separate method.
candidates.trigger: diff modifies an existing async hook method so that it returns a different structure or traverses more than the previous implementation, without a new parameter to opt in

candidates.rule: Process-wide singleton pools must not implement `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` context-manager protocol unless they own a truly scoped lifecycle; use an explicit lifecycle hook instead.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `__aenter__` / `__aexit__` to a class that stores itself in a module-level `_instances` dict (singleton pattern)

candidates.rule: When a provider notifier adds version-gated behaviour via `AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS`, evaluate whether the guard belongs in `BaseNotifier` rather than duplicated in every concrete notifier.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS:` version guard inside a concrete `Notifier.__init__` or `notify()` method

candidates.rule: Before calling `response.raise_for_status()` against a provider API, log the error response body so that upstream error messages are preserved for debugging.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `response.raise_for_status()` without a preceding log statement that captures the response body on 4xx/5xx

candidates.rule: Hard-coded timeouts for long-running provider API calls (e.g. agent or ML model requests) must be exposed as a configurable operator/hook parameter rather than a module-level constant.
candidates.trigger: diff introduces a module-level `*_TIMEOUT` constant that gates an HTTP request to a long-running provider API (ML/agent/query workloads) without a corresponding constructor parameter

candidates.rule: Push deferrable-operator query/job identifiers to XCom immediately after they are obtained, before entering the poll loop, so they survive task failure.
candidates.trigger: diff moves an `xcom_push` call for query/job IDs to after a polling loop in a deferrable operator's `execute` or equivalent method

candidates.rule: Use `try/except ImportError` instead of `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS` guards when importing symbols that moved between `airflow.sdk` and `airflow.providers` or `airflow.sensors`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `if AIRFLOW_V_x_y_PLUS: from airflow.sdk... else: from airflow.sensors...` or similar SDK/provider import split

candidates.rule: Use the ContextVar token/reset pattern (set → try/finally → reset) for every Airflow ContextVar mutation, matching the precedent set by initdb().
candidates.trigger: A ContextVar is assigned via .set() but no token variable is stored and no corresponding .reset(token) call exists in a finally block.

candidates.rule: Do not use caplog in tests; assert observable behaviour or return values, not log output.
candidates.trigger: A test imports or uses caplog (pytest's log-capture fixture) to assert on logged messages.

candidates.rule: SecretsMasker exception-chain traversal tests must include a cross-circular case (exc1.__cause__ = exc2; exc2.__context__ = exc1) to verify the visited-set guard works for mixed __cause__/__context__ cycles.
candidates.trigger: Tests for circular exception chain handling only cover same-attribute cycles (__cause__/__cause__ or __context__/__context__) but not the cross-attribute cycle.

candidates.rule: Task-SDK documentation examples that show async @task functions must include a complete @dag-decorated wrapper so the example is a runnable DAG file.
candidates.trigger: A .rst or .md docs example defines an @task-decorated function and calls it at module level without an enclosing @dag-decorated function.

candidates.rule: The pre-commit hook test suite for check_provide_session_kwargs must cover the bypass path where an allowlist entry is removed or newly added (not only the 'loosen count' path).
candidates.trigger: Tests for _expand_for_allowlist_edits only exercise the case where an existing entry's count is increased, without a test where an entry is removed from or added fresh to known_provide_session_positional.txt.

candidates.rule: Pre-commit hook tests must pass resolved paths (Path.resolve()) matching the production hook's path-normalization behaviour.
candidates.trigger: A test for a pre-commit hook passes a raw Path or string where the production code calls Path(f).resolve() before comparison, causing the test to use non-normalised paths.

candidates.rule: MetricsMap implementations must use a consistent key strategy across all instrument types, or use separate sub-maps per instrument type, to prevent slot collisions between gauges and histograms.
candidates.trigger: A MetricsMap (or equivalent shared metrics registry) keys different instrument types (gauge, histogram, counter) using different key schemes (one uses name alone, another uses name+tags), or stores all instruments in the same dict.

candidates.rule: Name async variants of existing methods with the 'a' prefix (e.g., aget_connection), not an 'async_' prefix.
candidates.trigger: A new async classmethod or method is named async_<something> where a synchronous counterpart <something> already exists.

candidates.rule: When a new config-driven default is introduced on a class, add a regression test that changes the relevant config key before constructing the object and asserts the default is read correctly.
candidates.trigger: A class __init__ reads a config value (e.g., conf.getfloat) to supply a default for an argument, but no test constructs the class after modifying that config section/key.

candidates.rule: Local imports used to break a circular dependency must have a comment identifying the circular dependency being avoided; prefer module-level imports otherwise.
candidates.trigger: A local (function- or method-body) import exists without an adjacent comment explaining why it cannot be a module-level import.

candidates.rule: Entries added to airflow/sdk/__init__.py __all__ and the lazy-import dict must be inserted in alphabetical order.
candidates.trigger: A new symbol is appended to the __all__ list or the lazy-import dict in task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/__init__.py without being placed in the correct alphabetical position.

candidates.rule: In the Java coordinator, register stdout/stderr socketpair pipe readers before the connection accept loop starts, not after.
candidates.trigger: A subprocess coordinator calls _accept_connections (or equivalent selector-based accept loop) before calling _register_pipe_readers (or equivalent) on the socketpair write-ends passed to the subprocess.

candidates.rule: Language-agnostic coordinator plumbing (_start_server, _accept_connections, socketpair setup) must live in BaseCoordinator, not be duplicated per language coordinator.
candidates.trigger: A new language coordinator under task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/ re-implements socket server startup or connection-accept helpers that are not specific to that runtime.

candidates.rule: Each language coordinator's constructor arguments need only make sense for its own runtime; coordinators do not need matching argument signatures.
candidates.trigger: A language coordinator is given arguments whose names or types are copied to match a different coordinator rather than being idiomatic for that runtime.

candidates.rule: SecretsMasker tests for exception-redaction paths must assert that chained exceptions (__context__ / __cause__) are also redacted, not merely that the primary exception is handled.
candidates.trigger: A test for _redact_exception_with_context_or_cause (or equivalent) only checks exc.args and does not attach a __context__ or __cause__ containing a secret to verify chain traversal.

candidates.rule: Within task-SDK coordinator modules, use `exc_info=True` as a structlog keyword argument instead of `error=str(exc)` when logging caught exceptions at debug/warning level, so the traceback is preserved for debuggability.
candidates.trigger: log.debug(..., error=str(exc)) or log.warning(..., error=str(exc)) inside task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/

candidates.rule: Do not define a separate `__version__` attribute inside `airflow.sdk.coordinators.*` sub-packages; the canonical distribution version is exposed only at `airflow.sdk.__version__`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `__version__ = "..."` or `"__version__"` in `__all__` inside task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/*/

candidates.rule: All datetime fields placed into a callback context dict must be wrapped with `coerce_datetime` (from `airflow.sdk._shared.timezones`) to produce `pendulum.DateTime` objects, consistent with `RuntimeTaskInstance.get_template_context()` and the triggerer-side context builder.
candidates.trigger: diff populates a context dict in callback_supervisor.py with datetime fields from DagRunResult or similar without calling coerce_datetime()

candidates.rule: When renaming message types in `comms.py`, update the message-type sync test allowlists in `airflow-core/tests/unit/dag_processing/test_processor.py` and `airflow-core/tests/unit/jobs/test_triggerer_job.py` in the same PR.
candidates.trigger: diff renames a class in task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/comms.py that appears in ToTask or ToSupervisor without updating the corresponding hardcoded allowlists in test_processor.py or test_triggerer_job.py

candidates.rule: Partition keys accumulated for the same task instance must be stored as a set (deduplicated), not a list, consistent with how asset aliases handle repeated keys.
candidates.trigger: diff uses a list field (e.g. attrs.field(factory=list)) for partition_keys on a task-instance context object and appends without deduplication

candidates.rule: In Asset lookup code, treat `Asset(uri=...)` as having `name == uri` (matching the DB storage convention), and do not treat `name=None` as a meaningful distinct state from `name=uri`.
candidates.trigger: diff introduces None-guarded name/uri paths in Asset or AssetRef handling inside task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/context.py without normalising name to uri when name is absent

candidates.rule: Import `NotRequired` (and other symbols added in later Python minor versions) with a `try/except ImportError` stdlib-first fallback before importing from `typing_extensions`, to support the full Python version range Airflow targets.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a bare `from typing_extensions import NotRequired` (or similar backport) without a stdlib try/except guard

candidates.rule: Function-local imports are only permitted when a circular import makes a module-level import impossible; otherwise move all imports to module scope.
candidates.trigger: diff adds an import statement inside a function body where the same module is already imported at the top of the file or no circular-import comment explains the deferral

candidates.rule: Task-SDK mapper classes exported in the public API must fully implement all abstract methods of their base class (including `to_upstream()`); incomplete implementations must be kept abstract or unexported until finished.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a concrete mapper class in task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/partition_mappers/ that inherits RollupMapper without overriding to_upstream()

candidates.rule: When a Task-SDK API method (e.g. `Variable.keys()`) only queries the metadata database and does not consult secrets backends, the docstring must include an explicit `.. note::` block documenting the asymmetry with `Variable.get()` and why secrets backends are excluded.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a Variable.keys() or similar listing method in task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/variable.py without a note about secrets-backend exclusion

candidates.rule: Exception classes defined in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/exceptions.py` that are only raised (and not caught) within the Task SDK must not be imported into `airflow-core`, even in tests; tests for those exceptions must reside in the SDK test tree.
candidates.trigger: diff imports an exception from airflow.sdk.exceptions inside airflow-core source or airflow-core/tests/

candidates.rule: The `supervise_callback` function must call `_make_process_nondumpable()` before spawning a subprocess, exactly as `supervise_task` does, to prevent core dumps from leaking secrets present in callback credentials (Notifier tokens, connection passwords, etc.).
candidates.trigger: diff adds or modifies a supervise_callback function in callback_supervisor.py without a call to _make_process_nondumpable()

candidates.rule: When invoking a callback callable with context kwargs, only pass `context` when `accepts_context` returns True AND the context value is not None; never forward `context=None` to a callback.
candidates.trigger: diff passes **callback_kwargs unconditionally to callback_callable when accepts_context() is True, without checking context is not None

candidates.rule: Exception log calls inside `callback_supervisor.py` must include structured identifying fields (`callback_id=`, `pid=`) to distinguish concurrent callback failures in logs, mirroring the `ActivitySubprocess` pattern in `supervisor.py`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds log.exception(...) or log.error(...) in callback_supervisor.py without callback_id or pid keyword arguments

candidates.rule: Warning and API error text that tells a task author how to offload an oversized stored value must name the worker-side `[workers] state_store_backend` option, not the server-side `[state_store] backend`; keep the same section name in the asset-store warning and in the API error messages.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a size-limit warning or HTTP error message in task-sdk execution_time code that names a `[state_store]` config option as the remedy for a too-large value

candidates.rule: When instantiating a user-configured coordinator via `import_string(spec.classpath)(**spec.kwargs)`, catch `ImportError`/`TypeError` and re-raise with the offending coordinator key and classpath, and assert `isinstance(coordinator, BaseCoordinator)` before caching the instance.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `import_string(<spec>.classpath)(**<spec>.kwargs)` for a config-driven plugin/coordinator without error wrapping or a base-class check on the result

candidates.rule: When client-level exception translation replaces an existing error path (e.g. HTTP 409 becoming `TaskAlreadyRunningError`), do not delete the supervisor-level end-to-end test: add a replacement asserting that `ActivitySubprocess.start()`/`supervise` raises the new exception and that the child process is killed.
candidates.trigger: diff removes a test from `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/execution_time/test_supervisor.py` while adding equivalent coverage only in `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/api/test_client.py`

candidates.rule: Tests that keep a task subprocess alive to exercise signal delivery must bound their worst-case runtime to tens of seconds; do not write operator bodies like `for i in range(1000): sleep(1)`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a test operator whose `execute` loops with `sleep(...)` for a worst-case total duration well beyond a minute

candidates.rule: Use `partition_key` only for exact-match asset-event filtering; any regex or pattern value (e.g. one starting with `^`) must be passed through `partition_key_pattern`, in production code and in test cases alike.
candidates.trigger: diff sets `partition_key=` to a value containing regex metacharacters in a `GetAssetEventByAsset` message or asset-event query

candidates.rule: A regression test for a new `sys.exit(...)` inside `run()` must assert more than `SystemExit(1)`: it must also verify that `on_failure_callback`, the `on_task_instance_failed` listener, and `email_on_failure` still fire for the failed task instance.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a task-runner test asserting only `pytest.raises(SystemExit)` / an exit code for a failure path introduced by a new `sys.exit()` call in `run()`

candidates.rule: New language-SDK task registration APIs should follow the two-step registration the Java and Go SDKs use — define the callable, then register the task against a Dag — so Dag-level arguments stay expressible when whole-Dag definition in the language SDK lands; an inline `registerTask({dagId, taskId}, fn)` must be justified against that forward path.
candidates.trigger: diff adds or documents a task registration entrypoint under `ts-sdk/` that binds dagId and taskId inline in a single call

candidates.rule: Every `Socket` the ts-sdk coordinator creates must register an `error` handler at construction time that writes the channel name and message to stderr; an unhandled socket `error` event takes down the Node task process.
candidates.trigger: diff constructs or stores a `Socket` under `ts-sdk/src/coordinator/` wiring only `data`/`close`/`connect` handlers

candidates.rule: Client-side socket reconnection in a language SDK is only correct if the Airflow coordinator accepts a second connection on the same channel; when adding `scheduleReconnect`/backoff logic, verify and cover the coordinator-side re-accept path in the same PR.
candidates.trigger: diff adds reconnect or backoff logic to a ts-sdk coordinator socket, e.g. `sock.on("close", ...)` calling `this.scheduleReconnect()`

candidates.rule: A secrets backend cannot enforce a denial by raising an exception alone: the backend-iteration loops (`_get_connection`, `_async_get_connection`, `_get_variable` in `execution_time/context.py`, and the same pattern in `models/connection.py`) use bare `except Exception: continue`, so any new deny signal must be special-cased and re-raised there in the same change.
candidates.trigger: diff makes a secrets backend raise `PermissionError` (or another auth-denied exception) without changing the `except Exception` backend-fallthrough loops to re-raise it

candidates.rule: In supervisor message handlers, do not guard task-SDK API client results with `isinstance(resp, XResponse)` plus an `else` branch: client methods return their response model unconditionally and raise `ServerResponseError` on failure, so call `XResult.from_api_response(resp)` directly like the neighbouring handlers do.
candidates.trigger: diff adds an `isinstance(<resp>, <X>Response)` check with an `else` fallback around a `self.client.<resource>.<method>(...)` call in `supervisor.py`

candidates.rule: Never print or log a `Connection` object, a `ConnectionResult`, or the output of `Connection.get_uri()` in task-SDK execution paths — including temporary debug prints left in a PR.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a `print(...)` or logging call that interpolates a `Connection`, `conn_result`, or `get_uri()` under `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/`

candidates.rule: Imports of private third-party internals (e.g. `from structlog._output import WRITE_LOCKS`) in the supervisor must be wrapped in `try/except ImportError` with a `None` fallback, and every use guarded (`if WRITE_LOCKS is not None:`), so a dependency upgrade that moves or removes the internal cannot break task execution.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a module-level import of an underscore-prefixed module or attribute from a third-party package under `task-sdk/src/`

candidates.rule: Tracing helpers that no-op below a configured OTel detail level must return `contextlib.nullcontext(trace.INVALID_SPAN)` rather than `trace.INVALID_SPAN` itself, so `__enter__`/`__exit__` always exist and `with detail_span(...) as span` still yields `INVALID_SPAN`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a span wrapper whose disabled branch returns `trace.INVALID_SPAN` while `__enter__` calls `self._ctx.__enter__()`

candidates.rule: Do not wrap conn-id filesystem injection for `ObjectStoragePath` in a blanket `except Exception: pass`; set the cached filesystem through `self.fs` so failures are consistent, and either let the exception propagate or suppress only the specific provider-not-available / scheme-unregistered errors while logging at debug.
candidates.trigger: diff assigns `attach(...).fs` to `__wrapped__._fs_cached` (or similar) guarded by a bare `except Exception: pass` in `sdk/io/path.py`

candidates.rule: Mocks of the task-SDK execution API `Client` in task-sdk tests must be specced — `MagicMock(spec=Client)`, `spec_set`, or `create_autospec` — including nested attributes such as `task_instances`, rather than a bare `MagicMock()`.
candidates.trigger: diff adds `client = MagicMock()` / `fake_client = MagicMock()` under `task-sdk/tests/` and then sets `<mock>.task_instances.<method>.return_value`

candidates.rule: A comment that tells readers to run a benchmark or helper script must name an entrypoint that exists in the tree (e.g. under `dev/`); otherwise add the script in the same PR or drop the instruction.
candidates.trigger: diff adds a comment or docstring pointing at a `dev/...` script (or other repo entrypoint) that is not present in the repository
